canonical.name: Tensor-product test density and coefficient uniqueness
canonical.support: Local Fourier-series and polarization proof supplies this prerequisite in full; Fredenhagen–Rejzner motivate the regular coefficient-kernel model but do not supply this density argument.

canonical.name: Diagonal delta test functional and its exact support
canonical.support: The A-page helper proves the diagonal trace functional is continuous and supported exactly on the thin diagonal; the B-page remark uses this exact interface.

sources.title: Klaus Fredenhagen and Katarzyna Rejzner, Perturbative algebraic quantum field theory, complete lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete 42-page full text, §§4–7; regular/local functionals, contraction product and normal ordering, time-ordered products, causal factorization, and the local extension discussion.

contents.name: §4: Regular polynomial functionals and smooth compactly supported derivative kernels
contents.support: The local definition fixes finite symmetric smooth compact coefficient kernels and explicitly identifies the regular class.

contents.name: §4: Local functionals with diagonal-supported higher derivatives
contents.support: The B-page remark gives a direct quartic example of the regular/local distinction and verifies its diagonal distribution.

contents.name: §5: Star product from contractions of regular functional derivatives
contents.support: The item extends the source formula to continuous bidistributions and supplies full domain, continuity, and associativity proofs.

contents.name: §5: Change of two-point kernel and normal-ordering map
contents.support: The item proves the finite distributional contraction identity for a symmetric kernel shift.

contents.name: §6: Time-ordered products and causal factorization
contents.support: The definition supplies the finite regular contraction coefficients and fixes the exact relative-kernel lift and conventions.

contents.name: §6: Formal S-series causal factorization
contents.support: The theorem proves the coefficientwise identity conditionally from the inspected free scalar carrier interfaces.

contents.name: §7: Extension of time-ordered products to local functionals
contents.reason: The extension requires scaling-degree and local extension-space prerequisites assigned to the planned qft-ir04 pair; this batch records the obstruction for regular kernels only.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete 42-page text and the full arguments in §§4–7, including the regular/local distinction, contraction formula, normal-ordering map, causal factorization condition, and local extension caveat.
source_review.supports: Regular functional scope, contraction and normal-ordering formulas, causal factorization context, and the need for a separate local extension.
source_review.limitations: The local proofs here supply the distributional continuity, coefficient-kernel topology, complete combinatorics, and exact free scalar conventions; the source formulas are not treated as proofs of those details.

sources.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, complete author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes, Chapter 3
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML Chapter 3; §3.1.1 on Dyson time ordering and §§3.3.1–3.3.2 on Wick expansion and contractions, including equations (3.221)–(3.245).

contents.name: §3.1.1: Dyson series and time ordering
contents.support: The local theorem adds strong-continuity hypotheses, a vector-integral construction, operator-norm bounds, uniqueness, unitarity, and factorization to the source’s formal series.

contents.name: §3.3.1: Wick expansion and contractions
contents.support: The local theorem extends the finite contraction pattern to arbitrary regular polynomial kernels and proves associativity.

contents.name: §3.3.2: Four-field contraction coefficients
contents.support: The B example computes the k=0, k=1, and k=2 terms with coefficients 1, 4, and 2.

contents.name: §3.3: Normal ordering and contraction identities
contents.support: The local lemma proves the exact kernel-change isomorphism beyond the source’s generator-level Wick identities.

source_review.read_extent: Read complete HTML Chapter 3, including §3.1.1 and §§3.3.1–3.3.2 and their displayed Dyson/Wick derivations.
source_review.supports: The Dyson ordering structure and finite Wick contraction coefficients used as independent QFT context.
source_review.limitations: The local operator theorem proves the analytic convergence claims; the local regular-functional theorems prove all distributional-domain and extension details.
